title: Diagram Scene Protocol Scene Schema
description: Draft JSON Schema for the canonical DSP scene document. Licensed under Apache-2.0; the spec and both schemas are at https://github.com/zindexai/diagram-scene-protocol.

extensions.description: Reserved extension point for protocol additions. Recognized keys include `showLifelineFeet` (sequence diagrams only) and `autoGroup` (architecture diagrams only).

showLifelineFeet.description: Sequence-diagram only. When true (default), the renderer draws a foot bar at the bottom of each lifeline mirroring the head (UML / PlantUML / Mermaid convention). Set to false to suppress foot bars - useful when the author authors their own bottom row of shapes.

autoGroup.description: Architecture-family only. When set, the engine synthesizes subtle background bands grouping nodes by their `nodeType` (e.g. one band for all `service` nodes, one for `database` nodes, one for `externalSystem` nodes). Each band is labeled with the pluralized type name ("Services", "Databases", "External Systems"). Skipped when the scene already authors frames containing the candidate nodes (no double-wrap), when all nodes share a single `nodeType` (trivial), or when the nodes of a type are scattered (a node of another type sits between two of them in a column). Opt-in only; omit the field to render with no banding (existing default).

diagramFamily.description: Diagram family declaration. Technically optional in the schema but effectively load-bearing: gates family-specific validation, layout, and rendering behavior the engine and downstream tooling rely on (sequence-family fan-in exemption, ER auto-promote-fk-labels, workflow BPMN conventions, family-namespaced node types). Without it the diagram is drawn as a generic flowchart, and nothing warns you. Always declare on every scene.

layoutStrategy.description: How the engine places the nodes that have no position. The engine picks its placement method from diagramFamily: a layered layout for architecture, workflow, entityRelationship and uiflow diagrams and for diagrams without a family, which read these fields; a tree for orgchart (top to bottom), forces for network, and message order for sequence, which don't. A field left out takes the layered layout's default.

direction.description: Layout direction: top to bottom, bottom to top, left to right, right to left.

nodeSpacing.description: Pixels the engine aims for between nodes in the same rank. Not a minimum: when it lays out every node it also tries tighter and wider spacings and keeps the layout that scores best, and it widens gaps to fill a larger canvas.

rankSpacing.description: Pixels the engine aims for between adjacent ranks. Not a minimum: when it lays out every node it also tries tighter and wider spacings and keeps the layout that scores best, and it widens gaps to fill a larger canvas.

palette.description: Scene-level color palette that overrides theme defaults for unstyled elements. All properties optional - only specify the colors you want to override. Cascade: element style > palette > theme > fallback.

accentPrimary.description: Accent color of nodes whose style sets no accentColor: ER table headers and PK badges, org chart card stripes, UI flow screen and modal title bars

accentSecondary.description: Nothing draws a second accent yet, so this has no effect

color.description: CSS-compatible color string. Implementations may choose to restrict this further.

metadata.description: Freeform metadata for provenance or custom annotations.

rotation.description: Kept with the layout. The reference engine doesn't rotate anything.

units.description: The units of every position and size. Only px.

id.description: The diagram's ID. Zindex sets it when the diagram is created through /v1/diagrams or diagram_create, ignoring any value sent.

brief.description: Context kept with the diagram for the next agent: what it shows, conventions to keep, decisions made. Versioned with the diagram.

extensions.description: Not kept: the reference engine drops it when it stores the diagram. Put data in the document's top-level extensions instead.

grid.description: Kept with the diagram. The reference engine draws no grid.

snap.description: Kept with the diagram. The reference engine doesn't snap to a grid.

viewport.description: Kept with the diagram. The reference engine doesn't read it.

sceneDefaults.description: Kept with the diagram. The reference engine doesn't read these: set fonts, strokes and routers on elements or in styles.

zIndex.description: Paint order: higher draws on top. When absent, the engine assigns one by kind, counting up in array order within each kind: frames from 0, groups from 100, edges from 200, nodes from 300, text from 400, images from 500 and guides from 600.

locked.description: Kept with the element. The reference engine edits and draws an element whatever its value.

visible.description: false hides the element: the engine still lays it out, so it keeps its space, but doesn't draw it or any edge with an end at it. A hidden frame hides only its box and title, and a hidden group only its title, not their members.

oneOf.description: Reference to a named style in scene.styles

style.description: Element style: either a named-style string key (resolved against scene.styles) or an inline StyleValue object

columns.description: ER table columns, read by er.entity and er.weakEntity nodes. Each column draws as a row; an edge anchors at a row with endpoint.column, and an edge end left without cardinality is inferred from the column's flags. updateNode replaces the whole array.

operator.description: A sequence fragment's operator (a frame whose containerType is fragment): alt, opt, loop, par, break, critical, neg or ref, drawn in its tab as written.

operands.description: A sequence fragment's operands after its first, top to bottom. Each starts at one of the fragment's rows (startsAt, a message or note id, after its first row) and may carry a guard; a dashed divider is drawn above that row, for every operator, with the guard under it in brackets the renderer adds. The first operand is the fragment's own, with the frame's title, drawn as written, as its guard. An operand with a y is refused; a version stored with one still draws, each such operand at the first message or note drawn at or past its y.

startsAt.description: A sequence.activation's first message: the bar starts at that message's arrow, on the lifeline it arrives at.

endsAt.description: A sequence.activation's last message: the bar ends at that message's arrow. Without it, the bar is as tall as one row at startsAt.

x.description: Shorthand for layout.x - sets layout.mode to 'absolute' automatically

y.description: Shorthand for layout.y - sets layout.mode to 'absolute' automatically

width.description: Shorthand for layout.width - sets layout.mode to 'absolute' automatically

height.description: Shorthand for layout.height - sets layout.mode to 'absolute' automatically

startsAt.description: The row the operand starts at: a message or note inside the fragment, after its first row.

guard.description: The operand's guard, drawn in brackets after its divider.

erColumn.description: One column of an ER table (er.entity, er.weakEntity): drawn as a row with its PK/FK badges and type.

name.description: Column name, drawn on its row. endpoint.column, and an edge label that names a foreign key, match it.

type.description: Column type, drawn right-aligned on the row.

pk.description: Part of the primary key. An edge end at the only PK column infers one; at one of several, many.

fk.description: A foreign key. An edge end here infers many: one when unique (or the entity's only PK column), zero-or-many when nullable, zero-or-one when both.

unique.description: Unique on its own: a unique foreign key infers one.

nullable.description: Nullable: a nullable foreign key infers zero-or-many, or zero-or-one when unique.

key.description: Alias for pk: true or fk: true. A column that is both needs pk and fk.

comment.description: Kept with the column (a Mermaid attribute comment), not drawn.

autoSize.description: 'content' sizes a node whose label wraps (textStyle.wrap 'word' or 'character') to its text: it keeps this width and gets at least the height its wrapped label and icon need, the height a TEXT_OVERFLOW warning gives, growing down from its top edge. The height here is the minimum. Nodes it grows into move down to make room, keeping the full spacing from it: the node spacing in a left-to-right flow, the rank spacing (80 px by default) in a top-to-bottom one. No effect on a label set to 'auto' or 'none' (the engine already sizes that node to it) or on nodes that lay out their own text: org chart people and roles, UI flow screens and modals, ER tables with columns, sequence nodes, BPMN events and gateways, UI flow entry and exit points.

layout.description: Position and size. Leave it out and the engine places the node next to its neighbors, around the nodes that have a layout, and sizes it to its content. After the first save the engine records the position here and keeps it, unless a node that grows needs the room and pushes this one, a node an edit adds needs more room for its edge label than the column it joins and this node is in that column or beyond it, an edit adds or deletes a frame round it and keeping it would leave frames overlapping or a frame holding a node that isn't its member, or an added order constraint finds its two nodes the wrong way round; the autoLayout op, and a new or removed layoutStrategy or diagramFamily, place nodes again. Sequence diagrams are laid out from their messages, so their nodes stay at x 0, y 0. A layout at exactly x 0, y 0 counts as not placed.

icon.description: Icon key ({family}:{id}, e.g. lucide:database) or URL

router.description: How the edge is drawn. `orthogonal`, the default when `router` is left off (and `polyline`, drawn the same), is right-angle segments the engine routes round other nodes where a route exists. `straight` is one line between the two nodes' centers, ending where it crosses each node's outline. `curved` is one bowed arc between the two nodes, ending on each outline; a lone curve bows to the side that clears other nodes where one does, and curves between one pair of nodes spread into a lens. Neither `straight` nor `curved` is routed round nodes: one that runs through a node gets the warning EDGE_CROSSES_NODE. Sequence messages ignore `router`.

anchor.description: Where this end of the edge meets its node: `side` alone fixes the side, and the end sits where the engine spreads ends on that side; with `offset` it sits at that place, 0 to 1 from the top of a left or right side or the left of a top or bottom side, kept 8 px from the side's corners. An anchored edge joins no shared trunk. The engine doesn't move nodes for it, so an anchor on the side facing away from the other node routes round the node. Ignored, with EDGE_ANCHOR_IGNORED, on a sequence message, a self-loop, or an end that names a column.

side.description: The side of the node this end meets.

offset.description: Where on the side, 0 to 1 from its top (left and right sides) or its left (top and bottom sides). Omit it to let the engine place the end on the side.

endpoint.description: Edge endpoint. elementId may reference any element kind - typically a node, but frame and group IDs are also valid targets. An edge to a frame terminates at the frame's border, on the side facing the source, straight across where the source lines up and otherwise at the side's center; useful for abstract group dependencies (e.g. an edge to a 'Regional Services' sidebar rather than to a specific service inside). On entityRelationship diagrams, set `column` to anchor the edge at a specific column row inside the entity (matching the dbdiagram.io / DBeaver convention where FK edges point at the FK column itself rather than the entity rectangle as a whole).

column.description: Optional column-row anchor for ER entities. When set, must match the `name` of a column declared in the endpoint entity's `extensions.columns` array. The edge's segment touching this endpoint anchors at the column row inside the entity instead of the entity's outer face. Mismatched names emit an EDGE_COLUMN_NOT_FOUND warning.

cardinality.description: ER-style cardinality marker for this endpoint. Omitted, it is inferred from the column the end anchors at each time the diagram is drawn, and isn't stored, so it follows the column.

edgeEndpoints.description: Arrowheads at each end. An arrowhead left out comes from the edge's edgeType: workflow.messageFlow has an open circle at the source and an open triangle at the target, sequence.async and sequence.reply an open triangle at the target, and every other type, default included, a filled triangle at the target and none at the source.

label.description: Edge label text. Plain strings render as a single tspan. Labels matching the state-machine / SCXML / BPMN convention 'EVENT [guard] / action' render with multi-tier typography: event 12px, guard 10px muted, action 10px muted italic. Detection is content-based (balanced [...] OR ' / ' separator) and family-agnostic. Multi-line labels (containing \n) skip the convention parse.

waypoints.description: Kept with the edge, but not drawn: the engine routes every edge itself and doesn't pass through these points.

edgeType.description: Family-specific edge type for typed connection semantics

layout.description: A frame's box. A sequence fragment's is ignored: a fragment is laid out with its rows.

containerType.description: Semantic container type for swimlane and process layout

laneDirection.description: Direction for lane-based layout within this container

wrap.description: 'auto', a node's default, keeps the label on one line while its node can grow to hold it, up to 250 px of content (wider if the layout gives more); a longer label wraps by word there and the node grows taller. On a text element, 'auto' wraps by word when the text is wider than its box. 'none', a text element's default, breaks lines only at \n, and a node grows as wide as the line. 'word' also wraps at spaces to fit the width, and a word wider than the width runs past it. 'character' wraps at spaces too and breaks such a word between its characters.

align.description: Horizontal alignment. When absent: center on a node, left on a text element.

verticalAlign.description: Vertical alignment. When absent: middle on a node, top on a text element.

accentColor.description: Accent color: the header and PK badges of an ER table, the stripe of an org chart card, the title bar of a UI flow screen or modal

color.description: Alias for textColor (normalized to textColor at runtime)

forceLabel.description: Edge-only: draw the edge's label where the engine would leave it out. When an edge's label exactly matches the name of a column declared in either endpoint's extensions.columns, the edge anchors at that column's row inside the entity (the dbdiagram.io / DBeaver convention) and the label isn't drawn, because the row carries the FK identity. Set this to true to draw the label as well: the edge still anchors at the column, and its cardinality at that end is inferred from the column.

id.description: Optional. Unique among the document's constraints when given: removeConstraint removes a constraint by its id.

columns.description: Elements per row; the elements fill as many rows as they need.

elements.description: Each element is centered in the container on both axes.

labelWidth.description: Measured label width including padding. Used by the renderer to draw a background rect behind edge labels.

router.description: How the renderer draws `points`. `"curved"` only for an edge whose own `router` is `curved`: the 2-point points list is drawn as the quadratic Bezier `M points[0] Q control points[1]`. Every other edge is drawn as a polyline; the engine never turns an orthogonal edge into a curve, and a long back-edge detour becomes an orthogonal U-hook below the diagram instead.

control.description: A curved edge's quadratic Bezier control point. The engine picks the side and depth of the curve and puts its ends on the nodes' outlines; the curve is `M points[0] Q control points[1]`. A curved path without it, laid out by an earlier engine, is drawn with its control point 30% of the chord off the chord's middle, left of travel.

cornerRadius.description: Engine-applied corner-rounding radius for the polyline path: a sequence diagram's self-message and a curved self-loop are drawn as a U with rounded corners.

isFanInFeeder.description: True when this edge is a feeder of a shared port: one of several edges that enter one port of their target and join one trunk there (a flowchart decision's face, which one flow line enters; a face with no room to keep them apart; edges whose shared label is drawn once). Its last point is the junction, on the last leg of the edge that carries `junctions`, off the target's face, and it draws no arrowhead.

junctions.description: Set on the edge whose last leg, the trunk, carries a shared port's joined edges into the target with one arrowhead: every point where the joined edges' lines branch: where the feeders meet the trunk, and where one feeder's line meets another's on the way there. The renderer draws a filled dot at each.
